key_insight: The paper argues that AI/ML in turbulence modeling works best when matched to the flow’s regime, using a complexity map in Reynolds number and non-equilibrium to decide between ML-RANS, scale-resolving simulation, and PINNs.
engineering_relevance: For CFD practice, this provides a physics-based deployment guide that can reduce wasted compute and prevent applying learned closures outside their valid flow domain.
method: Build a turbulence taxonomy map using degrees of freedom (Re) and non-equilibrium (SK/ε).
Apply Weaver’s complexity framework to separate flow regimes by physical complexity.
Use the map to match each regime to the appropriate modeling strategy: ML-RANS, SRS, or PINNs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that prior AI/ML turbulence efforts have shown only modest progress, with ML-RANS often failing to generalize and SRS often being computationally prohibitive.
watch_item: The framework is conceptual rather than a new benchmarked algorithm, so its practical value depends on correctly diagnosing the flow regime before choosing a model.
paper_title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Complex Systems Perspective
